name: tetraptych
title: Waku, four ways
text: The same orca, four flat palettes, one grid: a straight Warhol repetition, Ben-day dots standing in for the print screen he never actually ran through.

name: rising-sun
title: Waku, rising sun
text: Red and white, radiating: the flag-field treatment, not the flag itself. Kanji stamp reads 波, nami — wave, the thing Waku is named for.

name: great-wave
title: Waku, the great wave
text: A hand-drawn homage, not a reproduction: Hokusai's silhouette, simplified to three flat shapes, indigo and gold, Waku riding the crest instead of a fishing boat.

name: kabuki
title: Waku, kabuki paint
text: Kumadori face-paint stripes borrowed for the mask, not the man: red courage-lines on black, magenta ground, the Ben-day dot standing in for woodblock grain.

name: nine-up
title: Waku, nine ways
text: A 3x3 grid instead of the tetraptych's 2x2: the same Warhol repetition pushed one step further, nine flat hues cycling warm to cool, newsprint dot screen under each cell.

name: strip-four
title: Waku, four in a row
text: A 1x4 strip of vertical bands, not a square grid: four duotone panels, cream line holding each apart, the repetition read left to right instead of in a block.

name: sixpack
title: Waku, six up
text: A 2x3 grid, six panels: a pastel half-step away from the tetraptych's primaries, checkerboard ground standing in for the print screen this time instead of dots.

name: diptych
title: Waku, two ways
text: One canvas split down the middle, day against night: the smallest repetition grid in the set, a single hard edge instead of a ruled line between panels.

name: tri-panel
title: Waku, three ways
text: A vertical triptych, dawn to dusk: three flat sky tones in sequence rather than a gradient doing the work, the orca held identically in each panel.

name: pod-formation
title: Waku, the pod
text: Not a grid: one large orca and four small ones in loose formation, the Warhol repetition broken into a scatter instead of a block, Ben-day dots for water texture.

name: seigaiha-field
title: Waku, wave scales
text: Seigaiha, the nested-arc wave-scale field, behind the orca instead of a plain ground: four rings per tile, a simplification of the traditional hand-overlapped version.

name: asanoha-field
title: Waku, hemp leaf
text: Asanoha, the hemp-leaf geometric field, worn thin behind the orca: one six-line star repeated per tile, a simplification of the full interlocking lattice, indigo on gold.

name: ichimatsu-field
title: Waku, checkerboard
text: Ichimatsu, the two-tone checkerboard, full bleed: the orca in flat red on top of the field instead of inside a panel of it, the field doing the pop-art repetition instead of a grid of orcas.

name: newsprint
title: Waku, newsprint
text: A halftone dot screen in three offset plates, cyan, magenta, black, like a misregistered comic print: bolder and coarser than the Ben-day dots used elsewhere in the set.

name: red-fuji
title: Waku, red Fuji
text: A homage to Hokusai's Red Fuji, not a copy: the mountain reduced to one flat red triangle and a white snow-cap wedge, Waku breaching where the print has only sky.

name: evening-rain
title: Waku, evening rain
text: A homage to Hiroshige's rain-streak woodblocks, simplified to a field of straight diagonal lines over a dark indigo ground, the orca surfacing through them.

name: villain-paint
title: Waku, blue paint
text: A second kumadori palette: blue and indigo stripes, the color kabuki convention reads as menace rather than the red courage-lines used for the hero role in the first piece.

name: sorrow-lines
title: Waku, sorrow lines
text: A third kumadori palette: purple, downward-sweeping lines instead of the upward courage-lines, the convention for grief or nobility rather than heroism or menace.

name: sakura-shower
title: Waku, cherry blossom
text: A sakura shower: simplified five-petal blossoms scattered at three sizes over the orca, the petals rendered as plain ellipses rather than the notched botanical form.

name: indigo-sun
title: Waku, indigo sun
text: The rising-sun composition again, split-complementary this time: indigo field and gold rays instead of red and white, the same radiating field-treatment logic.

name: gold-leaf
title: Waku, gold leaf
text: Mostly negative space: one flat gold disc, an ink outline of the orca and nothing else, the minimal end of the register against the busiest pieces in the set.

name: gold-tide
title: Waku, gold tide
text: A sibling to the gold-leaf piece with one shape added: a single flat indigo wave under the same ink-line orca, on a gold ground instead of cream.

name: umi-stamp
title: Waku, umi
text: The kanji stamp enlarged from a corner seal to the whole ground: 海, umi, sea, filling the field the orca sits on instead of marking a signature in the corner.

name: deep-stamp
title: Waku, deep
text: The same enlarged-glyph treatment as the umi piece, a different word: 深, deep, dark navy ground standing for the water the orca is under rather than on.

name: noren
title: Waku, noren
text: A shop-curtain (noren) treatment: two panels hung from a header bar with a slit between them, the orca's head passing through the gap as if walking under it.

name: inverse-wave
title: Waku, the wave, inverted
text: A literal color inversion of the great wave piece: gold ground, indigo where the foam was, a straight negative read of the same three flat shapes.

name: inverse-kabuki
title: Waku, kabuki paint, inverted
text: A literal color inversion of the kabuki piece: cream ground, black courage-lines, the magenta pushed down to the eye patches instead of filling the field.

name: moonlit
title: Waku, moonlit
text: The rising-sun field at night: a pale moon instead of a red sun, moonbeam wedges confined to the upper half instead of a full radiating circle, silver-grey orca.

name: rough-water
title: Waku, rough water
text: An original storm composition, not a print homage: bold black wave-crests on indigo, high contrast, the orca breaching through rather than riding a named crest.

name: horizon-bands
title: Waku, horizon bands
text: A leaping pose against flat horizon bands instead of a sky gradient: five discrete warm tones stacked like a Rothko field standing in for a sunset.
